feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: Strikes between U.S. and Iran continue as hostilities intensify
entry.summary: The U.S. has launched more strikes at Iran, one day after the two countries exchanged fire for the first time in a month

entry.title: Ex-National Security Council advisor on the latest strikes between the U.S. and Iran
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep asks retired Rear Admiral and Biden administration National Security Council advisor John Kirby about the latest exchange of fire between the U.S. and Iran.

entry.title: He died of 'natural causes.' But his mother says she knows what killed him: heat
entry.summary: When Arizona counts heat-related deaths, Adam Willson isn't included. His story shows how thousands of heat deaths can go uncounted every year in the United States.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: U.S. military strikes rock Iran for a second day in a row, Trump attempts to combat rising gas prices as midterm approaches, Sen. Ed Markey wins Massachusetts' Democratic primary.

entry.title: Author Rozina Ali's new book explores the roots of Islamophobia in the U.S.
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with journalist and author Rozina Ali about her new book, "Seasons of Fury: Four Families and the Rise of Islamophobia in America."

entry.title: Whistleblower claims USPS plan for Trump's mail voting order could disrupt midterms
entry.summary: An anonymous federal official warned in a whistleblower complaint that a technical system the Postal Service built for mail voting is flawed and, if implemented, likely to disrupt the fall midterms.

entry.title: Whistleblower's lawyer warns USPS plan for Trump's order could keep ballots from voters
entry.summary: A lawyer for an anonymous whistleblower says Postal Service plans for an unusual verification rule, combined with a hastily built online system, could delay mail ballots from reaching eligible voters.

entry.title: Advocates say cities' aggressive clearing of encampments has caused more problems
entry.summary: A Supreme Court ruling two years ago allowed bans on sleeping outside. Homeless people and advocates in the Midwest say aggressive encampment clearing has caused problems.

entry.title: Octavia Butler's 'Survivor' returns to print nearly 50 years after its release
entry.summary: "Survivor," a novel taken out of print at the request of author Octavia Butler, returned to print this week.

entry.title: Trump attempts to combat high gas prices as affordability crisis looms over midterms
entry.summary: President Trump seems to be pulling out all the stops to mitigate high gas prices ahead of the midterms.
